rules.quote: Don’t use blogs for essential information that should be stand-alone content.
rules.specification: The page does not define which information is essential or requires stand-alone treatment. This needs an editorial decision.
rules.violation_condition: A blog post contains essential information that should instead be presented as stand-alone content.
rules.why: G-1: retain the specific content restriction rather than the broader planning heading.

rules.quote: Don’t duplicate information that’s available elsewhere.
rules.specification: The scope of ‘elsewhere’ and the amount of overlap that counts as duplication are not specified. A comparison scope and duplication criterion need to be agreed.
rules.violation_condition: A blog post duplicates information already available elsewhere.
rules.why: Grain test: duplicating existing information is a different issue from publishing essential information in the wrong content type.

covers.quote: But make sure you have something useful to say.

rules.quote: A blog post should solve users’ problems or answer their questions.
rules.violation_condition: A blog post neither helps solve a user problem nor answers a user question.
when: Either helping solve a problem or answering a question satisfies the requirement.
rules.why: G-4: the specific user-purpose requirement absorbs the broader instruction to have something useful to say.

parts.quote: How to get mental health support
Tips for making a grant application
Need support? Here’s what you need to know
Get your application in now – time is running out

rules.quote: Start with a title that helps users understand what the post is about.
rules.violation_condition: A blog post does not start with an informative title identifying what the post is about.
rules.why: G-4: consolidate the repeated title-clarity requirement; keyword inclusion and clickbait remain separately stated checks.

rules.specification: Interpret keywords as words or phrases naming the post’s main subject or user task. The page supplies no mandatory keyword list.
rules.violation_condition: A blog post’s title contains no keywords identifying its main subject or user task.
rules.why: Grain test: keyword inclusion is an explicit title requirement, distinct from the broader requirement for an informative title.

rules.specification: The examples illustrate unsuitable teaser, promotional and urgency-based titles, but the page does not define the boundary between clickbait and legitimate descriptive or time-sensitive wording.
rules.violation_condition: A blog post has a clickbait title.
rules.why: Grain test: a title can identify its topic and contain keywords while still using clickbait.

covers.quote: Organise content with a clear structure using section headings.

rules.quote: Break up your post with headings
rules.violation_condition: A blog post presents its body as an unbroken run of prose without section headings.
rules.why: G-4: consolidate the repeated requirement for section headings; paragraph length and heading wording are separate checks.

rules.quote: Order headings from most to least important.
rules.specification: The relative importance of the topics must be established; the page does not provide ranking criteria.
rules.violation_condition: The headings in a blog post put less important topics before more important topics.
when: Applies to the ordering of headings in blog posts.
rules.why: Grain test: topic ordering is distinct from whether headings exist or describe their sections.

rules.quote: Cover one main idea per paragraph.
rules.violation_condition: A paragraph develops more than one main idea.
when: Applies to paragraphs in blog posts.
Supporting details about the same main idea do not constitute additional main ideas.
rules.why: Grain test: paragraph focus and paragraph sentence count can fail independently.

covers.quote: Break up your post with headings and short paragraphs.

rules.quote: Keep paragraphs to a maximum of 2 to 3 sentences so people can read them on mobile devices.
rules.specification: Interpret ‘a maximum of 2 to 3 sentences’ as an upper limit of 3 sentences, not a requirement that every paragraph contain at least 2 sentences.
rules.violation_condition: A paragraph in a blog post contains more than 3 sentences.
when: Applies to paragraphs in blog posts.
rules.why: G-4: the explicit sentence limit makes the earlier short-paragraph instruction actionable; E-4 makes the interpretation visible.

parts.quote: Ever wanted to know what to do when hosting an ideas challenge? Our case studies open up a world of ideas and translate them into practices you can apply at work.

rules.quote: Use a warm and conversational tone in your blog posts.
rules.violation_condition: A blog post’s tone is not warm and conversational.
rules.why: Grain test: tone is an independent property of the post; the following sentence explains its benefit rather than adding a rule.

rules.quote: This is the first thing a screen reader user will hear and should align with the first heading on the page.
rules.specification: Interpret alignment as agreement in topic and purpose, rather than requiring identical wording. ‘This’ refers to the page title in the preceding sentence.
rules.violation_condition: A blog page’s page title does not align with its first heading.
rules.why: Grain test: title-to-heading alignment is distinct from the clarity of either text in isolation.

rules.quote: Clearly describe the topics or the following section in the headings.
rules.violation_condition: A section heading does not clearly describe the topic or content of the section that follows it.
when: Applies to section headings in blog posts.
rules.why: Grain test: descriptive heading wording is a separate check from the presence or ordering of headings.

covers.quote: Unless images are for decorative purposes, describe the visual information in alt text.

rules.quote: Write alternative text that describes the information or function of the image.
rules.violation_condition: A non-decorative image lacks alternative text conveying its information or function, including when alt text is missing entirely.
when: Applies to images in blog posts.
rules.why: G-2/G-4: consolidate the repeated meaningful-alt-text requirement and retain the decorative-image exception.

parts.quote: To bookmark the topics you find most useful, visit the Style Manual.

rules.quote: Include a call to action at the end of your post.
rules.violation_condition: A blog post does not end with a call to action.
when: The listed types of invitation are examples, not a requirement to include every type.
rules.why: G-4: use the actionable body sentence rather than the descriptive heading; the following list illustrates possible calls to action.
